full_judgment: 4. Being aggrieved by the notice, the petitioner filed appeal being No.65 of 2007 before the Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal on 22-1-2007 under Rule 13 of the Valuation Rules, 2000. Tribunal vide notice dated 14-1-2008 directed the petitioner to comply with the provisions of section 194 of the Customs Act directing to deposit fine through Bank Guarantee and cash. After receiving the notice the petitioner filed an application on 23-1-2008 before the Tribunal stating that the petitioner filed appeal against the fixation of value under Rule 13 of the Valuation Rules and no fine was imposed upon the petitioner as such section 194 of the Customs Act is not applicable in this case and also requested the Tribunal to admit the case for hearing without direction to deposit fine amount. The Tribunal fixed 24-1-2008 for hearing on the point of limitation and depositing money under section 194 of the Customs Act. Though the Tribunal fixed hearing at 10-00 am and the learned advocate for the petitioner waited till 1-30 pm but the Tribunal did not resume and, as such, learned lawyer filed an application for adjournment but the Tribunal without considering the bonafide cause stated in the application rejected the application and also dismissed the appeal for not taking step vide impugned order dated 24-1-2008 which is reproduced below:
